bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Proprietary GMP 360 technology stack of seven purpose-built platforms sharing a common intelligence layer and core engine, allowing innovation to scale across the A3 ecosystem
- AI-first product architecture with in-house neural-network and machine-learning models driving real-time targeting, bidding, inventory selection and campaign execution
- Revenue quality from durable enterprise relationships: direct clients accounted for 73.9% of revenue, rather than lower-margin volume routed through intermediaries
- Asset-light, cloud-native operating model paired with outcomes-as-a-service pricing, allowing unit economics to improve as the Company grows (EBITDA margin 20.8% versus 16.5% in the previous year)
- India-based global capability model that can serve higher-value international markets without a matching rise in cost; revenues in both INR and USD provide a natural currency hedge
- Scale of data and reach: 125 Cr+ signals processed daily, ~250 Cr devices reached worldwide, 100+ Cr monthly impressions and 25,000+ campaigns delivered across branding and performance
- Privacy-first, device-agnostic and omnichannel architecture with an advanced ID graph and HouseSync connected-household targeting, and 30+ interactive/premium ad formats
- Talent depth and retention: 200+ professionals across the Group including technology entrepreneurs and industry leaders with over 100 years of combined management expertise, supported by the ESOP 2025 scheme
- Industry recognition including DIGIXX Summit Awards 2026 AI-Powered Consumer Growth Platform of the Year and Best Demand-Side Platform of the Year, and Adgully DATAMATIXX 2025 Best AI Tech Agency of the Year and Best Data-Driven Marketing Platform for PrsmX
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Regulatory and data-privacy change in digital advertising — MD&A lists this as a threat: the digital advertising industry operates within an evolving regulatory and policy environment where changes to data privacy, digital governance, consumer protection and advertising standards may influence industry practices and compliance requirements. Because the entire revenue base is digital advertising delivered on consented consumer data, a tightening of consent or data-protection rules directly constrains the targeting capability the platforms are built on.
- Sector-specific regulation can remove demand at short notice — the Real Money Gaming precedent — The Chairman states that 'Regulatory changes affecting the Real Money Gaming (RMG) segment created near-term headwinds' in FY 25-26. This is the concrete, already-realised version of the regulatory risk: a rule change in one advertiser vertical withdraws spend immediately, and the Company has no contractual protection against it.
- Signal loss — third-party cookie deprecation, ATT and consent fragmentation — The Chairman describes the broader ecosystem evolving through tighter privacy regulations and the gradual deprecation of third-party cookies. Loss of deterministic user-level signals erodes the identity and retargeting basis of platforms like SurgeX and ResurgeX, forcing continuous reinvestment in contextual, probabilistic and first-party approaches simply to hold performance constant.
- Rapid technological change and competitive intensity in adtech — MD&A flags that the adtech industry evolves rapidly, driven by advances in AI, automation, changing consumer behaviour and new media channels, and that these shifts can reshape competitive dynamics, technology standards and advertiser preferences. Technology obsolescence is also named as an external risk factor under the Risk Management Policy; the transition from AI-assisted to AI-autonomous decisioning means an incumbent stack can be leapfrogged rather than gradually eroded.
- Global market and currency exposure — MD&A flags that operating across multiple markets exposes the business to changing economic conditions and foreign exchange movements. The Company argues the mix of INR and USD revenues is a natural hedge, but international revenue is being scaled deliberately (11.5% of FY 25-26 revenue, with the UK launched during the year), so this exposure grows with the strategy.
- Demand is tied to advertiser budgets, which are cyclical and confidence-linked — MD&A concedes that advertising budgets 'are still closely tied to business confidence and consumption', against an IMF backdrop of global growth slowing to 3.1% in 2026 with risks tilted to the downside — a longer or wider Middle East conflict, geopolitical fragmentation, renewed trade frictions and any reassessment of expectations around AI-led productivity. A single-segment advertising business has no counter-cyclical revenue line.
- Concentration: one reportable segment, a direct-client-heavy book and a small set of growth verticals — For the year under review the Company operated in a single reportable business segment; direct clients accounted for 73.9% of revenue and growth was led by Quick Commerce, BFSI, Fintech and Retail, with the business still anchored in India (international only 11.5%). Revenue quality is high, but the exposure is undiversified by segment, by client type and by geography, so a downturn in a few large advertiser categories transmits straight to the top line.
- Trust, brand safety and ad fraud in the inventory supply chain — The Chairman notes advertisers expect transparency and brand-safe environments while consumers expect data to be handled responsibly, and that the Company is 'consistently fortifying our proprietary technology with AI-driven fraud detection, intelligent brand safety mechanisms and rigorous inventory quality controls'. The Risk Management Policy separately names third-party and reputational risk categories — a fraud or brand-safety failure on bought inventory is both a client-loss and a reputational event.
- Dependence on proprietary technology and on specialised engineering talent — The Risk Management Policy names protection of proprietary information, operational efficiency and human resource management among internal risk factors. The moat is the in-house GMP 360 stack and the engineering, ML and data-science people who build it; the Company introduced the ESOP 2025 scheme specifically to attract and retain specialised talent, which marks retention as a recognised pressure point.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body: Founded in 2010 as Lucent Industries Limited, an education-focused enterprise, the Company has evolved into an AI-native adtech and marketing-technology business that plans, delivers and measures digital advertising for brands. Its offering is delivered through the proprietary GMP 360 technology stack, organised around the A3 framework of Awareness, Acquisition and Activation, and priced on an Outcome-as-a-Service (OaaS) basis that shifts the focus from media delivery to verified consumer outcomes. It operated in a single reportable business segment during the year, serving direct advertisers and agencies across banking, retail, consumer goods, quick commerce, fintech, travel and OTT.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Build an AI-native consumer growth platform rather than another advertising technology company, prioritising tangible consumer outcomes across Awareness, Acquisition and Activation over impressions
- Operate to the 'Rule of 50' long-term operating framework: annual revenue growth of more than 30% together with EBITDA margins above 20%
- Vision 2030: build a globally scalable, AI-native platform from India that competes across both emerging and developed markets
- Strengthen AI capabilities and invest in contextual intelligence, diversified signal processing and predictive optimisation, on the view that the future relies less on identity-based targeting and more on relevance, contextual understanding and real business outcomes
- Expand international presence — the UK operation launched during the year and Latin America was expanded further — served from the India-based global capability model
- Invest in technology that reinforces long-term competitive advantage while maintaining disciplined capital allocation
- FY 26-27 is about scaling what has been built, with discipline, consistency and long-term conviction
- Deepen domestic wallet share with large enterprise clients and build a scalable mid-market business through sector-led solutions, cross-selling and agency partnerships
- Consolidate the group into one unified organisation: the integration of Mobavenue Media Private Limited and the renaming of the listed entity from Lucent Industries Limited to Mobavenue AI Tech Limited gave a sharper strategic identity
- Deliver through a single unified proprietary technology infrastructure — the GMP 360 stack of seven platforms sharing a common intelligence layer and core engine — so innovation scales across the A3 ecosystem
- Continue environmental and social initiatives across sustainability, healthcare and community development alongside commercial growth
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Mobavenue is an asset-light, cloud-native platform business, so expansion is platform build-out and geographic footprint rather than plant capacity. The Company describes its 'asset-light, cloud-native operating model' working alongside outcomes-as-a-service pricing so that unit economics improve as it grows. Growth investment is directed at the proprietary product stack — PrsmX, SurgeX, ResurgeX, DiscvrX, PiiX, OrbitX and AmplifiX — which share a unified proprietary technology infrastructure, and at the geographic footprint across India, ASEAN, MENA, LATAM, the UK and the USA, where international markets contributed 11.5% of revenue in FY 25-26 and can be served from the India-based global capability model without a matching rise in cost. The Board's Report states the Company continues to invest in strengthening technology capabilities, expanding AI-enabled product offerings and enhancing data-driven decision making, and that it will pursue continuous innovation and strategic investments in technology and talent. The only quantified forward commitment disclosed is a capital commitment of Rs 1,200 lakhs as at March 31, 2026 relating to the development of internally generated intangible assets (i.e. the platform/technology build), against Nil in the prior year; the Company states there are no other capital commitments as at that date.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Advertisers are concentrating disciplined budgets on channels with a clear, measurable return, which accelerates the shift of marketing investment towards digital, data-driven and AI-optimised formats — working in favour of technology-led players even where headline growth is subdued
- Global advertising spend passed US$1 Trillion in 2025 and is forecast at around US$1.06 Trillion in 2026, a growth of 5.0%, ahead of the 3.1% global GDP expansion projected by the IMF
- Digital channels account for close to 69% of spend across the 56 markets Dentsu tracks, and around nine in every ten additional advertising dollars now flow to online-only platforms
- The fastest-growing digital channels are the technology-led, measurable formats at the core of the Company's offering — retail media, connected TV, online video and social; retail media is forecast to grow 12.3% in 2026 while search moderates to 3.4%
- The marketing technology market is estimated at approximately US$223 Billion in 2026 and is expected to more than double by 2034; the broader adtech market is put in the region of US$0.9-1.1 Trillion in 2026 with double-digit annual growth projected to 2030
- In India digital advertising grew 26% to Rs 94,700 Crores, 63% of all advertising revenue, while television advertising declined by more than 10%; the media and entertainment sector is projected to reach Rs 3.3 Trillion by 2028 at a CAGR of over 7%
- India's digital advertising market grew 19% in 2025 to Rs 71,621 Crores and is projected to grow at a 17% CAGR to Rs 98,034 Crores by 2027, accounting for nearly 70% of total advertising spend
- Programmatic buying rose from 10% of India's digital advertising market in 2016 to 42% (Rs 30,081 Crores) in 2025 and is forecast at 43% in 2027
- India's digital economy has been expanding at roughly twice the pace of the wider economy, on a path towards approximately one-fifth of GDP by 2030, enlarging both the reachable consumer base and the pool of advertisers
- Demand during the year was led by direct advertisers with growing contributions from Quick Commerce, BFSI, Fintech and Retail; direct clients were 73.9% of revenue, reflecting durable enterprise relationships rather than lower-margin intermediated volume
- Operating leverage is the stated margin lever: the asset-light, cloud-native model with outcomes-as-a-service pricing lifted the EBITDA margin to 20.8% from 16.5%, allowing unit economics to improve as the Company grows
- International markets contributed 11.5% of revenue in FY 25-26, supported by the launch of UK operations and further expansion across Latin America; these are higher-value markets servable without a matching rise in cost
- Outcomes delivered rose through each quarter of the year, which management reads as evidence of platform scalability and of the fit between the Outcomes-as-a-Service model and client growth
- Advertisers are consolidating spend with partners that can show measurable outcomes across channels and are choosing integrated, full-stack platforms over single-purpose tools, pointing to a sustained multi-year runway for technology-led companies building globally scalable platforms from India
- Structural shift towards privacy-first, cookieless approaches and first-party data as ATT, browser restrictions on third-party cookies and stricter consent reduce deterministic user-level signals — favouring AI-led contextual targeting and probabilistic measurement
- Emergence of AI-native and agentic advertising: conversational interfaces and autonomous agents are moving AI from optimisation towards autonomous execution across planning, creative, targeting, bidding and measurement
- Open advertising ecosystems remain relevant at ~20-30% of global programmatic spends, with advertisers seeking alternatives to closed platforms offering greater transparency, interoperability and control
- Macro caution: the IMF projects global growth slowing to 3.1% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027 with risks tilted to the downside, including a longer or wider Middle East conflict, geopolitical fragmentation, renewed trade frictions and any reassessment of AI-led productivity expectations

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Advertisers are concentrating disciplined budgets on channels with a clear, measurable return, which accelerates the shift of marketing investment towards digital, data-driven and AI-optimised formats — working in favour of technology-led players even where headline growth is subdued
- Global advertising spend passed US$1 Trillion in 2025 and is forecast at around US$1.06 Trillion in 2026, a growth of 5.0%, ahead of the 3.1% global GDP expansion projected by the IMF
- Digital channels account for close to 69% of spend across the 56 markets Dentsu tracks, and around nine in every ten additional advertising dollars now flow to online-only platforms
- The fastest-growing digital channels are the technology-led, measurable formats at the core of the Company's offering — retail media, connected TV, online video and social; retail media is forecast to grow 12.3% in 2026 while search moderates to 3.4%
- The marketing technology market is estimated at approximately US$223 Billion in 2026 and is expected to more than double by 2034; the broader adtech market is put in the region of US$0.9-1.1 Trillion in 2026 with double-digit annual growth projected to 2030
- In India digital advertising grew 26% to Rs 94,700 Crores, 63% of all advertising revenue, while television advertising declined by more than 10%; the media and entertainment sector is projected to reach Rs 3.3 Trillion by 2028 at a CAGR of over 7%
- India's digital advertising market grew 19% in 2025 to Rs 71,621 Crores and is projected to grow at a 17% CAGR to Rs 98,034 Crores by 2027, accounting for nearly 70% of total advertising spend
- Programmatic buying rose from 10% of India's digital advertising market in 2016 to 42% (Rs 30,081 Crores) in 2025 and is forecast at 43% in 2027
- India's digital economy has been expanding at roughly twice the pace of the wider economy, on a path towards approximately one-fifth of GDP by 2030, enlarging both the reachable consumer base and the pool of advertisers
- Demand during the year was led by direct advertisers with growing contributions from Quick Commerce, BFSI, Fintech and Retail; direct clients were 73.9% of revenue, reflecting durable enterprise relationships rather than lower-margin intermediated volume
- Operating leverage is the stated margin lever: the asset-light, cloud-native model with outcomes-as-a-service pricing lifted the EBITDA margin to 20.8% from 16.5%, allowing unit economics to improve as the Company grows
- International markets contributed 11.5% of revenue in FY 25-26, supported by the launch of UK operations and further expansion across Latin America; these are higher-value markets servable without a matching rise in cost
- Outcomes delivered rose through each quarter of the year, which management reads as evidence of platform scalability and of the fit between the Outcomes-as-a-Service model and client growth
- Advertisers are consolidating spend with partners that can show measurable outcomes across channels and are choosing integrated, full-stack platforms over single-purpose tools, pointing to a sustained multi-year runway for technology-led companies building globally scalable platforms from India
- Structural shift towards privacy-first, cookieless approaches and first-party data as ATT, browser restrictions on third-party cookies and stricter consent reduce deterministic user-level signals — favouring AI-led contextual targeting and probabilistic measurement
- Emergence of AI-native and agentic advertising: conversational interfaces and autonomous agents are moving AI from optimisation towards autonomous execution across planning, creative, targeting, bidding and measurement
- Open advertising ecosystems remain relevant at ~20-30% of global programmatic spends, with advertisers seeking alternatives to closed platforms offering greater transparency, interoperability and control
- Macro caution: the IMF projects global growth slowing to 3.1% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027 with risks tilted to the downside, including a longer or wider Middle East conflict, geopolitical fragmentation, renewed trade frictions and any reassessment of AI-led productivity expectations

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin improved to 20.8% (FY26) from prior levels; supply/data cost remained flat at ~60% of revenue; employee cost up 20.1% YoY but disciplined relative to revenue growth; other expenses down 8.9% YoY

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: INR49.99cr preferential raise allocated to AI infrastructure, global expansion, and selective inorganic tech opportunities; disciplined approach; no dividends or buybacks mentioned

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Mobavenue is an asset-light, cloud-native platform business, so expansion is platform build-out and geographic footprint rather than plant capacity. The Company describes its 'asset-light, cloud-native operating model' working alongside outcomes-as-a-service pricing so that unit economics improve as it grows. Growth investment is directed at the proprietary product stack — PrsmX, SurgeX, ResurgeX, DiscvrX, PiiX, OrbitX and AmplifiX — which share a unified proprietary technology infrastructure, and at the geographic footprint across India, ASEAN, MENA, LATAM, the UK and the USA, where international markets contributed 11.5% of revenue in FY 25-26 and can be served from the India-based global capability model without a matching rise in cost. The Board's Report states the Company continues to invest in strengthening technology capabilities, expanding AI-enabled product offerings and enhancing data-driven decision making, and that it will pursue continuous innovation and strategic investments in technology and talent. The only quantified forward commitment disclosed is a capital commitment of Rs 1,200 lakhs as at March 31, 2026 relating to the development of internally generated intangible assets (i.e. the platform/technology build), against Nil in the prior year; the Company states there are no other capital commitments as at that date.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, forward-looking, disciplined; emphasis on AI-driven compounding, Rule of 50 (30%+ revenue growth, 20%+ EBITDA margin), and long-term value creation; tone reflects transition from legacy media broker to AI-native platform company

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Proprietary GMP 360 technology stack of seven purpose-built platforms sharing a common intelligence layer and core engine, allowing innovation to scale across the A3 ecosystem
- AI-first product architecture with in-house neural-network and machine-learning models driving real-time targeting, bidding, inventory selection and campaign execution
- Revenue quality from durable enterprise relationships: direct clients accounted for 73.9% of revenue, rather than lower-margin volume routed through intermediaries
- Asset-light, cloud-native operating model paired with outcomes-as-a-service pricing, allowing unit economics to improve as the Company grows (EBITDA margin 20.8% versus 16.5% in the previous year)
- India-based global capability model that can serve higher-value international markets without a matching rise in cost; revenues in both INR and USD provide a natural currency hedge
- Scale of data and reach: 125 Cr+ signals processed daily, ~250 Cr devices reached worldwide, 100+ Cr monthly impressions and 25,000+ campaigns delivered across branding and performance
- Privacy-first, device-agnostic and omnichannel architecture with an advanced ID graph and HouseSync connected-household targeting, and 30+ interactive/premium ad formats
- Talent depth and retention: 200+ professionals across the Group including technology entrepreneurs and industry leaders with over 100 years of combined management expertise, supported by the ESOP 2025 scheme
- Industry recognition including DIGIXX Summit Awards 2026 AI-Powered Consumer Growth Platform of the Year and Best Demand-Side Platform of the Year, and Adgully DATAMATIXX 2025 Best AI Tech Agency of the Year and Best Data-Driven Marketing Platform for PrsmX

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Global macro: geopolitical conflicts, oil price volatility, inflation; client concentration risk (no top client >10% disclosed); execution risk in global scaling; regulatory compliance in new markets

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Revenue per outcome increased 7.7% Q1 to Q4 (INR44.99 → INR48.44) — a hidden proxy for pricing power and AI efficiency; 125 crore daily signals processed and 50TB trained in 1hr — industrial-scale AI moat not visible in traditional metrics
